producer_report.summary: The race is fixed in the test only. The root cause was that the stand-in drain exited as soon as the stop file existed, so on a busy machine it was gone before the waiting stop_and_wait call looked. Now the stand-in leaves its loop only when both the stop file and a release file exist. The test passes a small Procs wrapper to the waiting call. The wrapper creates the release file right after the call's first process lookup, which has already seen the stand-in alive. The stand-in therefore always exits after the wait has begun, and no sleeps are involved. A new test reproduces the old shape: it releases the stand-in, reaps it, then calls the waiting stop, and asserts NotRunning(Dead(pid)). I kept production stop_and_wait unchanged on purpose. A dead pid that was never seen running cannot be told from a crashed or stale drain. Reporting Exited there could make `drain-stop --wait` claim a clean stop when the drain had already died, or when a stale pid file was left behind. I added one CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased / Fixed. I ran the drain tests (24 passed), fmt --check (clean) and the policy scan (17 passed). I did not run the full test suite or clippy.

checks_run.note: 24 passed, including the fixed test and the new one

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-cli status_and_stop_find_the_drain_by_pid_file`: the fixed test passes, and a new test that makes the stand-in exit before the waiting stop_and_wait call passes deterministically by asserting the old failure outcome NotRunning(Dead(pid)).
criteria_check.evidence: Ran the drain::tests module: the fixed test and the new a_stand_in_drain_that_exited_before_the_waiting_stop_reads_as_dead_not_exited both pass. The new test reaps the stand-in with wait() before the waiting call, so the outcome is deterministic. Caveat: the new test's name does not contain 'status_and_stop_find_the_drain_by_pid_file', so that exact filter runs only the fixed test; the new test needs its own name or 'drain::tests::'.

criteria_check.criterion: In the diff, the fixed test's stand-in does not exit on the stop file alone; it also waits for a release file that the test creates after the waiting stop_and_wait call has started, with no reliance on sleeps to win the race.
criteria_check.evidence: stand_in_drain loops while the stop file or the release file is missing. ReleaseAfterFirstLookup, a Procs wrapper, creates the release file right after the first start_marker lookup inside the waiting stop_and_wait. That lookup already returned alive, so the later poll sees the exit. No sleep is used to order events.

learnings: drain_state calls start_marker exactly once, so a Procs wrapper can hook the point between stop_and_wait's first look and its polling loop.
